passages.speaker: Arjuna / narrating voice
events: Arjuna is lured away from the field
Abhimanyu enters the formation alone
He is attacked by several commanders at once
passages.summary: One young warrior knows how to enter the formation but not how to leave it. He enters anyway when the opening appears, is separated from his allies, and is killed by several senior commanders acting together. The episode is a study of competence, isolation, and the ethics of a group deciding that one person's obligation excuses theirs.
passages.source_reference: Drona Parva — the chakravyuha and the death of Abhimanyu
passages.verification_note: Episode identity verified against the standard 18-parva division; `summary` is an editorial rendering, not a quotation.

passages.speaker: Arjuna
events: Arjuna swears to kill Jayadratha before sunset or immolate himself
Krishna helps him manage the daylight
passages.summary: After his son's death, Arjuna sets himself a deadline he knows may be impossible and declares that he will die on the field if he fails. Krishna's role in the episode is largely practical: he keeps the oath from destroying the man who made it. The passage shows grief converting into a commitment that must then be managed.
passages.source_reference: Drona Parva — Arjuna's vow after Abhimanyu's death
passages.verification_note: Episode identity verified against the standard 18-parva division; `summary` is an editorial rendering, not a quotation.

passages.speaker: Yudhishthira / Krishna
events: Krishna proposes that Drona be told the elephant Ashwatthama is dead
Yudhishthira adds an ambiguous clause
Drona lays down his arms
passages.summary: Drona cannot be defeated while he holds his weapons. Krishna proposes that he be told his son is dead; Bhima shouts it, and Yudhishthira, unable to speak the sentence outright, adds that it is so — and, it is said, that this is the one occasion on which his chariot did not rise from the earth. Drona lays down his arms and is killed. The episode is the epic's most careful examination of a half-truth told for a decisive advantage.
passages.source_reference: Drona Parva — the report about Ashwatthama
passages.verification_note: Episode identity verified against the standard 18-parva division; `summary` is an editorial rendering, not a quotation. The detail of the chariot sinking is a well-known narrative element of this episode.

passages.speaker: Krishna / Karna
events: Ghatotkacha fights at night and overwhelms the Kaurava army
Karna spends the weapon he had reserved for Arjuna
passages.summary: Krishna has been working to make Karna spend the one weapon that could kill Arjuna. When Ghatotkacha is killed by it, Krishna's relief is openly recorded. The text makes no attempt to hide that a good man's death was, from one vantage point, a successful expenditure — and lets that sit without resolving it.
passages.source_reference: Drona Parva — the fall of Ghatotkacha
passages.verification_note: Episode identity verified against the standard 18-parva division; `summary` is an editorial rendering, not a quotation.

passages.speaker: Karna
events: Karna defeats Yudhishthira
He tells him to withdraw from the war rather than be killed by him
passages.summary: Having defeated the man he has every reason to destroy, Karna orders him off the field instead of killing him. His stated reasons include his own standing and a debt to another. The decision costs him later, but the text records it as a real choice rather than an oversight.
passages.source_reference: Karna Parva — Karna's encounter with Yudhishthira
passages.verification_note: Episode identity verified against the standard 18-parva division; `summary` is an editorial rendering, not a quotation.

passages.section: Karna's wheel and the exchange with Krishna
passages.speaker: Karna / Krishna
events: Karna's chariot wheel sinks
He invokes the same rules the Pandavas earlier ignored
He is killed while calling for time
passages.summary: When his wheel is stuck, Karna demands the fairness he was never shown and points to what was done to Draupadi. Krishna answers by listing the same conduct as grounds for refusing him. Both are arguing from precedent; the text does not declare one of them correct and leaves the reader holding the contradiction.
passages.source_reference: Karna Parva — the death of Karna
passages.verification_note: Episode identity verified against the standard 18-parva division; `summary` is an editorial rendering, not a quotation.

passages.speaker: a Brahmin
events: Karna gives away what he has left when a stranger asks
He tells Krishna he has never refused a request
passages.summary: Karna's reputation for giving is tested to the point where he has nothing left, and he meets the test. Krishna later uses that history to make his case. The passage matters because it shows the very quality Karna is known for being the lever used against him.
passages.verification_note: Episode theme is well attested; the precise parva location of this exchange needs confirmation against the chosen edition before this passage may support a strong textual claim.

passages.speaker: Shalya / Karna
events: Shalya is made Karna's charioteer
He continuously undercuts Karna's confidence
passages.summary: A king who has been tricked into fighting for the other side is placed at the reins of the army's best warrior. He does his job while steadily telling Karna that he is not Arjuna's equal. The passage shows how an ally who does not believe in the cause can damage it from inside the same chariot.
passages.verification_note: Episode identity verified against the standard 18-parva division; `summary` is an editorial rendering, not a quotation.

passages.section: The last day and the fall of the kings
passages.speaker: narrator
events: Yudhishthira takes up command
Shalya is killed
The Kaurava army collapses
passages.summary: After days of delegating, Yudhishthira himself takes command on the final day and the opposing side disintegrates. The text marks the moment as a change in him rather than a change in strategy: the most reluctant of the five finally acts directly.
passages.source_reference: Shalya Parva — the final day of the war
passages.verification_note: Episode identity verified against the standard 18-parva division; `summary` is an editorial rendering, not a quotation.

passages.speaker: Ashwatthama
events: Ashwatthama enters the camp at night
He kills the sleeping commanders
Uttara's child is destroyed
passages.summary: Having lost his father and his cause, a man enters an enemy camp at night and kills those who cannot defend themselves. The text treats it as an atrocity rather than a retaliation, and follows it with punishment he must carry for the rest of his life. It is the clearest statement in the epic about where revenge ends.
passages.source_reference: Sauptika Parva — Ashwatthama's raid on the camp
passages.verification_note: Episode identity verified against the standard 18-parva division; `summary` is an editorial rendering, not a quotation.

passages.speaker: Krishna / Duryodhana
events: Duryodhana is offered a partition or five villages
He repeats that he will not give up what he has
passages.summary: Asked repeatedly to concede the smallest possible amount, Duryodhana says he would not give up a needlepoint of land. The text returns to this line after the war to show that everything that followed could have been avoided by the same concession he refused.
passages.source_reference: Udyoga Parva — Duryodhana's refusal of settlement
